deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are lecture notes for Grothendieck's IHES talks of Nov.–Dec. 1967. They became 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968). In §6, 'Calculs Čechistes', he computes the cohomology of the stratifying site of X/S by a Čech–Alexander complex.

Setup from the previous page. In the stratifying topos, the object X~ covers the final object. This gives a Čech–Leray spectral sequence
E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X~^{ν+1}, F)) ⇒ H^*(X_strat, F).
The product X~^{ν+1} is the ind-object 'lim→_i Δ^{(ν)}_X(i)'. Here Δ^{(ν)}_X(i) is the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{ν+1}, viewed as an object (U, X') of the site.

This page.
(1) For any object (U, X') of the site, H^*((U,X'), F) ≅ H^*(X', F_{(U,X')}). That is, cohomology of the topos localized at an object equals Zariski cohomology of the component sheaf on the thickening.
(2) Assume X is affine, so all Δ^{(ν)}(i) are affine. Assume the components F_{Δ^{(ν)}(i)} are quasi-coherent. A marginal addition also asks that they satisfy Mittag-Leffler. Then H^q(Δ^{(ν)}(i), F) = 0 for q > 0 by Serre vanishing on affines. Moreover, i ↦ H^0(Δ^{(ν)}(i), F) is a 'strict' projective system, meaning its transition maps are surjective.
(3) The cohomology of an ind-object is computed by a Milnor/R lim sequence: 0 → lim^1 H^{q-1} → H^q(lim→ Δ(i), F) → lim← H^q(Δ(i), F) → 0. By Mittag-Leffler the lim^1 term vanishes. Hence H^q(X~^{ν+1}, F) = 0 for q > 0, and H^0 = lim←_i F(Δ^{(ν)}_X(i)) = F(formal completion of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal).
(4) The Leray spectral sequence degenerates. For X affine and F with quasi-coherent components (e.g. F = O_{X_strat}):
H^*(X_strat, F) ≅ H^*(ν ↦ F((X^{ν+1})^_{/X})).
This is the cohomology of the cosimplicial module given by evaluating F on formal completions of the diagonals: the Čech–Alexander complex.
(5) The page then begins the non-affine case. The next page shows the outcome: a cosimplicial Zariski sheaf F^{(ν)}: U ↦ lim←_i F(Δ^{(ν)}_U(i)), together with H^*(X_inf, F) ≅ ℍ^*(X_zar, F^*) and a hypercohomology spectral sequence. After that he passes to the crystalline case in characteristic p, where X~ no longer covers the final object and one must embed X into a smooth scheme.
errors: The 'strict' (surjective) property of i ↦ F(Δ(i)) does not follow from quasi-coherence of the components alone. It needs the transition maps F_{Δ(i+1)} → F_{Δ(i)} to be surjective, which holds e.g. if F is a quasi-coherent crystal, or if one assumes Mittag-Leffler. Grothendieck seems aware of this: he adds 'et satisfassent Mittag-Leffler' in the margin, but the boxed statement only says 'quasi-cohérents'.

Formula (1), H^*((U,X'),F) ≅ H^*(X', F_{(U,X')}), is asserted without justification. It is standard (restriction to a localized topos plus exactness of evaluation on Zariski opens), so this is a minor gap only.
The identification of H^q of the ind-object with lim← H^q tacitly uses the lim^1 exact sequence. This is fine given the vanishing and strictness hypotheses.

ideas.what: Cohomology of the stratifying/infinitesimal topos of affine X computed by the cosimplicial module ν ↦ F(formal completion of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1968); developed further by Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Vanishing of higher cohomology of the ind-object X~^{ν+1} via Serre vanishing on affine thickenings plus Mittag-Leffler (lim^1 = 0).
ideas.modern_name: Milnor/R lim sequence with Mittag-Leffler vanishing

ideas.what: Globalization via a cosimplicial Zariski sheaf U ↦ F((U^{ν+1})^) and hypercohomology (begun here, completed on the next page).
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful draft of the standard Čech–Alexander computation that appears in Grothendieck's published 1968 'Crystals' lectures and in Berthelot's thesis. Nothing here is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: In the ind-limit expression, Grothendieck writes the formal colimit 'lim→_i' for X~^{ν+1}, and 'lim←' (arrow pointing left) for the limit of cohomology groups. This matches the transcription's ↓lim→ / lim← split, which is correct.
In the boxed formula, the crossed-out symbol under X^{(ν+1)}/ looks like '1⊠' or 'Δ' crossed out. The intended reading is 'X^{(ν+1)}/X, complété formel' (completion along the diagonal).
The phrase is '(p.ex. F = O_{X_strat})' rather than '(q.c. F = ...)': it gives an example of a sheaf satisfying the hypothesis.
The heading on the left of the previous page's last lines refers to 'Coh. stratifiante'. 'H^0(Δ^{(ν)}_X(i), F) pour i variable est un syst. proj. strict' is correctly read.
